regions.text: The most important item in this context is a database on agrochemicals per country, use,pending, as well as full registration. This project is currently under development. Theunderlying reason for these efforts is the role the ADl's (Acceptable Daily Intake) play inregulatory MRL's. This target has been approached by several avenues: (a) the amount ofagrochemicals sold (SIGMA database); (b) the extent of usage by farmers - an inquiry byUNITAB showed a distinct change of the usage pattern, and a surprisingly low number ofCPAs that are really in use; (c) a summary of the currently available toxicological reviews(I.T.I.C.).

A well-thought certification procedure was seen by ACAC as the most important topic ofthis chapter. Basic principles leading to a meaningful certification are: (a) use of labeled andregistered agrochemicals only; (b) effective communication to local growers' associations orgroups; (c) possibility to targeting the activities at growers' level, and (d) invoking thesupport of tobacco dealers.

An informational booklet was handed out to Argentinean tobacco farmers that showed in acolorful and easily understandable way the "do's" and "don't do's". It could serve as atemplate for similar booklets for other markets (Eastern Europe, Turkey). A cooperationwith the CORESTA Sub-Group on Good Agricultural Practice would have merits in thiscontext.

The most important issue in this context is a worldwide list of regulatory MRL's fortobacco. Such draft lists exist for some countries. However, due to the rapid development inthis sector, these lists are never exhaustive.

A discussion was held on the scientific meaning of MRL's since these numbers ratherbelong to a political category, though with some scientific background. Their counterpart inreality would be residues resulting from usage of agrochemicals according to GAP, thelatter being coined "GRL's" (Guidance Residue Limits).

ACAC has taken over the responsibility to overlook the situation dealing with GMtobaccos. The target of the committee is to get a worldwide overview over the recentdevelopments. ACAC will continue to keep CORESTA abreast of the latest developmentsin this field. The ACAC supports the development of quantitative methods for GMOdetection and determination by a specific Task Force.
Report of the Committee on Human Smoking Behaviour

Richard BAKER, Chairman of the Committee, reported on the progress of this Committee,which has nearly completed its work: the review on Compensation has been published in ascientific jourmal at the end of 1999, and presented as an inter-group paper by GerhardSCHERER at both 1999 Study Group meetings.
The review on vent blocking has been completed and is presently being submitted forpublication in a scientific journal.
